label: South and South-East Asia regulators
summary: Configures which State Bank of Pakistan, PISF, Central Bank of Sri Lanka or MAS regime binds the entity and in which variant (entity type, cloud or internet banking use, CII status, conditional modules, D-SIB status, notices followed); governance, critical systems, scores and incident reporting are the work after onboarding.

source.ref: Scope statements of the SBP, PISF, CBSL and MAS texts; each field names its own source

fields.label: SBP entity type

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 (ETGRMF scope) and the SBP cloud framework (regulated entities)

fields.note: The ETGRMF covers banks, development finance institutions and microfinance banks. The cloud framework also covers digital banks, e-money institutions and payment system operators and providers. SBP asks which one you are.

fields.label: Cloud use

source.ref: SBP Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers (BPRD Circular 01/2023)

fields.note: Whether any workload runs, or will run, with a cloud service provider. SBP's cloud framework covers outsourcing to cloud providers; with none it has nothing to cover. The workload list comes after onboarding.

fields.label: Offshore hosting

source.ref: SBP Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers (BPRD Circular 01/2023): offshore material workloads need SBP approval

fields.note: Whether any workload is, or will be, hosted outside Pakistan. SBP's cloud framework needs its approval for offshore material workloads, so hosting abroad adds requirements.

fields.label: Internet banking

source.ref: SBP Regulations for the Security of Internet Banking (Payment Systems Department)

fields.note: Whether the institution offers, or plans to offer, internet banking. SBP's security regulation covers institutions that do; if not offered it has nothing to cover. The systems that deliver it are scoped in Scope.

fields.label: PISF entity type

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site (research agent read the PDFs; document list re-checked)

fields.note: PISF applies to federal and provincial ministries and departments, autonomous bodies, corporations, CERTs and designated critical information infrastructure. It does not cover banks as such: choose Other if none fits, and ask the issuing authority.

fields.label: CII status

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: conditional CII Protection module

fields.note: PISF adds a 37-control module for designated critical information infrastructure. Designation comes from the authority, not from the organisation: if unsure, ask the sector regulator.

fields.label: Conditional modules

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: conditional modules Data Centre, Secure SDLC, CII Protection

fields.note: Three modules apply only in some cases: Data Centre (34 controls), Secure SDLC (10) and CII Protection (37), counted within PISF's 234 controls. Pick those that apply to the entity.

fields.label: Notified version

source.ref: PISF 2026 notification date and Gazette status could not be confirmed: reported as 13 Oct 2026 (approval 10 Aug 2026) while the nCERT page upload paths read 2026/03

fields.note: The PISF text and notification the entity works to. The notification date and Gazette status of PISF 2026 could not be confirmed (unverified); copy them from the nCERT page.

fields.label: Sri Lanka entity

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience (licensed banks)

fields.note: Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 is the current technology risk instrument for licensed banks; whether it supersedes the Baseline Security Standard is unverified. A finance company should confirm with CBSL which direction binds it.

fields.label: D-SIB status

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021: D-SIBs and other licensed banks are treated differently

fields.note: The Directions treat domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs) differently from other licensed banks. Say which group the bank is in; CBSL can confirm it.

fields.label: MAS entity type

source.ref: MAS Notice FSM-N05 (banks) and the MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines (January 2021)

fields.note: Notice FSM-N05 is the technology risk notice for banks; the Guidelines are issued to financial institutions generally. Other institutions should confirm with MAS which notice binds them.

fields.label: Notices followed

source.ref: MAS Notices FSM-N05 and FSM-N06, both effective 10 May 2024; Notice 655 status page (cancelled 10 May 2024)

fields.note: Notice 655 was cancelled on 10 May 2024 and replaced by FSM-N06; Notice 644 was replaced by FSM-N05 the same day. Do not cite the cancelled numbers.

source.ref: Regulator practice: whether an inspection, review or assessment already took place decides where the work starts. The option wording was written from the regulators' public circulars and was not checked line by line.

fields.label: Latest inspection
fields.note: Where the latest State Bank inspection of technology risk stands, if there was one.

fields.label: Inspection report
fields.note: Optional: attach the inspection report or letter. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Outsourced IT
fields.note: Whether critical IT services are outsourced. It tells which outsourcing requirements to review.

fields.label: Cloud providers
fields.note: The cloud providers in use or planned.

fields.label: Offshore approval
fields.note: Whether the State Bank approved hosting material workloads outside Pakistan.

fields.label: Approval letter
fields.note: Optional: attach the approval or acknowledgement. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Channels
fields.note: The internet banking channels in use or planned.

fields.label: Security review
fields.note: Whether the internet banking channels had an independent security review.

fields.label: Review file
fields.note: Optional: attach the review report. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Earlier assessment
fields.note: Whether an assessment against PISF, or an earlier national security framework, was done before.

fields.label: Assessment file
fields.note: Optional: attach the assessment report. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Latest CBSL review
fields.note: Where the latest Central Bank of Sri Lanka review of cyber security stands, if there was one.

fields.label: Review report
fields.note: Optional: attach the review report or letter. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Earlier TRM review
fields.note: Whether the technology risk controls were reviewed before, by internal audit or an external firm.

fields.label: Review file
fields.note: Optional: attach the review report. It is kept in Evidence.

fields.label: Cloud use
fields.note: Whether cloud services support the in-scope systems.

gate.label: The ETGRMF covers this entity type
gate.hint: SBP's 2017 announcement names banks, development finance institutions and microfinance banks; other entity types should ask SBP whether the ETGRMF binds them.

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 on the ETGRMF

gate.label: The entity uses or plans cloud
gate.hint: SBP's cloud framework covers cloud outsourcing; with none it has nothing to cover.

gate.label: The entity offers internet banking
gate.hint: SBP's internet banking regulation covers institutions that offer it.

gate.label: A designated CII operator applies the CII module
gate.hint: Designated infrastructure needs the CII Protection module.

gate.label: The entity is a licensed bank
gate.hint: Directions No. 16 of 2021 are written for licensed banks; a finance company should ask CBSL which direction binds it.

gate.label: A bank follows the banks' technology risk notice
gate.hint: Notice FSM-N05 is the technology risk notice for banks; tick it, or confirm with MAS why it does not apply.
